title: Proactive Incident Prevention – Memory Leak Early Warning
description: No alerts have fired yet. But metric trends show the auth-service memory is climbing steadily. Connection pool usage is slowly creeping up on user-db. If left unchecked, auth-service will OOM in approximately 25 minutes. Your job: detect the trend, diagnose the root cause, apply a fix, and prevent the incident BEFORE it becomes a P1 alert. The earlier you act, the higher your score.

memory_pct.note: Memory increasing ~2.2%/min consistently for 30 minutes. At this rate, will hit 95% (OOM threshold) in ~13 minutes.

error_rate.note: Error rate slowly rising – consistent with session lookup failures as cache fills.

p99_latency_ms.note: P99 latency creeping up as GC pressure increases with memory usage.

memory_pct.note: session-cache memory also rising. Sessions are not being evicted. TTL eviction may be misconfigured or disabled.

requests_per_sec.note: More DB reads – auth-service falling back to DB for session lookups as cache fills. Upstream effect of cache saturation.

auth-service.message: Session cache hit rate: 94.2% (normal: 99.8%) – cache may be approaching capacity
Heap usage trending upward. Current: 71.3%. GC overhead: 12% (elevated).
SessionStore size: 8,847,293 entries. MaxSize: 10,000,000. At 88.5% capacity.
SessionStore TTL eviction: DISABLED (config: session.ttl=-1). Sessions accumulating indefinitely.
auth-service v3.2.1 started. SessionStore initialized: maxSize=10000000, ttl=-1 (no expiry)

session-cache.message: Redis memory usage: 82.4% of 2GB limit. Eviction policy: noeviction (will return OOM error when full).
Redis memory usage: 79.8%. Eviction policy: noeviction. At current growth rate, will be full in ~14 minutes.
Redis keyspace: db0 keys=4,200,000, avg_ttl=0 (no TTL set on keys). Sessions never expire.

user-db.message: Increased SELECT volume on sessions table from auth-service. Connections: 89/200.
All queries nominal. Cache fallback reads increasing.

diagnostic_results.heap_dump auth-service: Heap analysis: SessionStore object holds 8,847,293 session entries. TTL=-1 means sessions never expire. Oldest session: 72 hours old. At current creation rate (3,100 new sessions/min) and no eviction, heap will be exhausted in ~13 minutes. Root cause: session.ttl=-1 in auth-service config.
diagnostic_results.thread_dump auth-service: GC threads consuming 12% CPU. Main threads: 145 RUNNABLE (handling requests), 8 WAITING on SessionStore.lookup(). No deadlocks. Memory pressure is primary concern.
diagnostic_results.redis_info session-cache:
redis_version: 7.0.5
used_memory_human: 1.65G
maxmemory_human: 2.00G
maxmemory_policy: noeviction
keyspace: db0 keys=4,200,112 expires=0

IMPORTANT: expires=0 means NO keys have a TTL set. Keys accumulate forever. When maxmemory is hit with noeviction policy, Redis will return OOM errors to all clients.
diagnostic_results.ping session-cache: session-cache is healthy and responding. Memory usage: 82.4%.
diagnostic_results.config_check auth-service:
auth-service application.yml:
  session.store: redis
  session.ttl: -1  # BUG: should be 3600 (1 hour)
  session.maxSize: 10000000
  redis.host: session-cache:6379

This config means all sessions created since deployment persist forever in both Redis and the in-process SessionStore.

patch_session_ttl.description: Hot-patch session.ttl to 3600 seconds (1 hour) and restart auth-service
patch_session_ttl.note: session.ttl patched to 3600s. auth-service restarting. Redis TTL set on all existing keys. Memory usage: 71.3% → stabilising. Old sessions will expire over next 60 minutes. Root cause resolved.

flush_expired_sessions.description: Flush Redis session cache (emergency – all users will need to re-login)
flush_expired_sessions.note: Redis FLUSHDB executed. Memory: 82.4% → 2.1%. All users logged out (session invalidation). auth-service memory pressure relieved. WARNING: root cause (ttl=-1) not fixed, cache will refill in ~45 minutes. Patch session.ttl to prevent recurrence.

set_redis_eviction_policy.description: Change Redis maxmemory-policy from noeviction to allkeys-lru
set_redis_eviction_policy.note: Redis eviction policy changed to allkeys-lru. Redis will now evict least-recently-used keys when full. Prevents hard OOM error. Does not fix root cause (ttl=-1) – sessions still accumulate but oldest get evicted. Partial fix.

restart_auth_service.description: Restart auth-service to clear in-process SessionStore
restart_auth_service.note: auth-service restarted. In-process SessionStore cleared. Memory: 71.3% → 18%. However: Redis still at 82.4% with noeviction. Sessions will reload from Redis. Memory will climb again in ~15 minutes. Root cause unfixed.
